Bill number: HB1214
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1249
 By Yarbro

 HOUSE BILL 1214

 By Johnson

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49,
 relative to education.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1403, is amended by deleting

subsection (e) and substituting:

 (e)

 (1) A parent of a participating student:

 (A) Shall ensure that the participating student is annually

 administered all Tennessee comprehensive assessment program (TCAP)

 tests, or successor tests authorized by the state board of education, that

 are administered to a public school student in the same grade or same

 course subject as the participating student;

 (B) In grade eleven (11) shall ensure that the student is

 administered the examination that is administered to public school

 students in grade eleven (11) pursuant to § 49-6-6001(b)(1); and

 (C) In any of the grades kindergarten through three (K-3) shall

 ensure that the participating student is annually administered each of the

 three (3) Tennessee universal reading screeners, or universal reading

 screeners approved by the state board of education, as described in § 49-

 1-905(c), during each of the three (3) administration windows established

 by the department of education pursuant to § 49-1-905(c)(1).

 (2) A participating student's results on the tests administered pursuant to

 this subsection (e) must be reported to the parent of the student.

 (3) Students with disabilities who would have participated in the alternate

 assessment, as determined on the student's IEP, are exempt from the

 requirements in this subsection (e).

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-10-1404, is amended by adding

the following as new subsections:

 (d)

 (1) A participating school shall publish the school's lesson plans and

 syllabus for each class offered by the school, a current list of materials in the

 school's library collection, and the academic standards for each class offered by

 the school on the school's website.

 (2) As used in this subsection (d):

 (A) "Library collection" means the materials made available to

 students by the participating school, including materials made available to

 students as part of a course curriculum; and

 (B) "Materials" means books, periodicals, newspapers,

 manuscripts, films, prints, documents, microfilm, discs, cassettes,

 videotapes, video games, applications, and subscription content in any

 form.

 (e) A participating school shall ensure that all educators of the participating

 school hold a valid license to teach in a public school that is issued by the state board of

 education.

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2607(e), is amended by adding

the following as new subdivisions:

 (6)

 (A) Publish the school's lesson plans and syllabus for each class offered

 by the school, a current list of materials in the school's library collection, and the

 academic standards for each class offered by the school on the school's website;

 and

 (B) As used in this subdivision (e)(6):

 (A) "Library collection" means the materials made available to

 students by the participating school, including materials made available to

 students as part of a course curriculum; and

 (B) "Materials" means books, periodicals, newspapers,

 manuscripts, films, prints, documents, microfilm, discs, cassettes,

 videotapes, video games, applications, and subscription content in any

 form; and

 (7) Ensure that all educators of the participating school hold a valid license to

 teach in a public school that is issued by the state board of education.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2606(a)(1), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (1) As a condition of participating in the program:

 (A) Participating students must be annually administered the Tennessee

 comprehensive assessment program (TCAP) tests, or successor tests authorized

 by the state board of education, that are administered to a public school student

 in the same grade or same course subject as the participating student;

 (B) Participating students in grade eleven (11) must be administered the

 examination that is administered to public schools students in grade eleven (11)

 pursuant to § 49-6-6001(b)(1); and

 (C) Participating students in kindergarten through grade three (K-3) must

 annually be administered each of the three (3) Tennessee universal reading

 screeners, or universal reading screeners approved by the state board of

 education, as described in § 49-1-905(c), during each of the three (3)

 administration windows established by the department of education pursuant to §

 49-1-905(c)(1).

SECTION 5. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill would change testing, transparency, and teacher license rules for participating students and schools in two Tennessee school choice programs. The bill text cites sections 49-10-1403 and 49-10-1404 and sections 49-6-2606 and 49-6-2607, but it does not name the programs.

On testing, a parent of a participating student would have to make sure the student takes each year the TCAP tests (or successor tests approved by the state board of education) given to public school students in the same grade or course subject. A student in grade 11 would have to take the exam given to public school grade 11 students under § 49-6-6001(b)(1). A student in kindergarten through grade 3 would have to take each of the three Tennessee universal reading screeners, or screeners approved by the state board, in each of the three administration windows set by the department of education. Test results would have to be reported to the parent. Students with disabilities who would have taken the alternate assessment under their IEP would be exempt. Section 4 would make the same testing requirements a condition of participating in the program under § 49-6-2606(a)(1).

On transparency, a participating school would have to post on its website its lesson plans and syllabus for every class, a current list of the materials in its library collection, and the academic standards for each class. The bill defines "library collection" as materials made available to students, including as part of a course. It defines "materials" broadly, covering books, periodicals, films, video games, applications, and subscription content in any form.

On staffing, a participating school would have to make sure all its educators hold a valid license to teach in a public school issued by the state board of education.

The act would take effect July 1, 2025.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: On testing, a parent of a participating student would have to make sure the student takes each year the TCAP tests (or successor tests approved by the state board of education) given to public school students in the same grade or course subject.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the parent's duty, annual testing, authorized successor tests, and matching grade or course subject. The paragraph also states the alternate-assessment exemption.

assessments.summary_quote: A student in grade 11 would have to take the exam given to public school grade 11 students under § 49-6-6001(b)(1).
assessments.rationale: Identifies the required examination and grade, but does not convey that the parent must ensure its administration; the express parental duty is limited to TCAP testing.

assessments.summary_quote: A student in kindergarten through grade 3 would have to take each of the three Tennessee universal reading screeners, or screeners approved by the state board, in each of the three administration windows set by the department of education.
assessments.rationale: Covers the grades, screeners, alternatives, and administration windows, but omits the annual frequency and the parent's responsibility to ensure administration.

assessments.summary_quote: Test results would have to be reported to the parent.
assessments.rationale: Conveys mandatory parental reporting of the test results described in the paragraph.

assessments.summary_quote: Students with disabilities who would have taken the alternate assessment under their IEP would be exempt.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the disability-related exemption and its dependence on the student's IEP alternate-assessment determination.

assessments.summary_quote: On transparency, a participating school would have to post on its website its lesson plans and syllabus for every class, a current list of the materials in its library collection, and the academic standards for each class.
assessments.rationale: Covers all required website postings and their class-by-class scope. The introduction identifies both sets of amended school provisions.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill defines "library collection" as materials made available to students, including as part of a course. It defines "materials" broadly, covering books, periodicals, films, video games, applications, and subscription content in any form.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the library-collection definition and some material categories, but omits expressly included categories such as newspapers, manuscripts, prints, documents, microfilm, discs, cassettes, and videotapes.

assessments.summary_quote: On staffing, a participating school would have to make sure all its educators hold a valid license to teach in a public school issued by the state board of education.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the school's responsibility, coverage of all educators, license validity, public-school qualification, and issuing authority.

assessments.summary_quote: On transparency, a participating school would have to post on its website its lesson plans and syllabus for every class, a current list of the materials in its library collection, and the academic standards for each class.
assessments.rationale: Conveys every required posting for participating schools, with the introduction establishing that the summary covers both sets of amended provisions.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill defines "library collection" as materials made available to students, including as part of a course. It defines "materials" broadly, covering books, periodicals, films, video games, applications, and subscription content in any form.
assessments.rationale: Covers student-accessible and course materials, but the abbreviated materials definition omits newspapers, manuscripts, prints, documents, microfilm, discs, cassettes, and videotapes.

assessments.summary_quote: On staffing, a participating school would have to make sure all its educators hold a valid license to teach in a public school issued by the state board of education.
assessments.rationale: Fully conveys the licensing requirement, presented as applying to participating schools under both sets of provisions.
